reasons: Numeric warning signals (Beneish M, Dechow F, accruals, OCF/NI): 4 of 4 computable flags triggered. All four quantitative screens firing together is a strong earnings-quality signal: high accruals relative to assets, operating cash flow well below net income, and M/F scores in manipulator ranges.

Financial pressure: 2 of 4 present (from going concern, covenant problem, revenue/EPS-linked incentive pay, capital raise). This creates a motive and opportunity to manage earnings, consistent with the numeric flags.
Management turnover: 1 of 2 present (CEO/CFO change or interim CFO). Leadership changes in finance often come before or alongside reporting problems.

Transaction complexity: 3 of 8 present (e.g., over-time revenue, contract assets, related parties, acquisitions, inventory write-downs, customer concentration). This adds judgmental areas where misstatement can be hidden, but the burden is moderate.

Internal control and audit 0 of 4, corrections 0 of 3, investigations 0 of 3: no material weakness, adverse ICFR opinion, auditor change, restatement or regulatory/litigation flags. This mitigates the risk and keeps the score below the high range. Most of the risk comes from the numeric and pressure signals rather than confirmed control failures.
